Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body: Hi Ankha, care to elaborate on difference between Khin not being triggered and mentioned Hackerspace being triggered by AC short appearance?

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> KoRneeshon wrote:
> Hi Ankha, care to elaborate on difference between Khin not being triggered and mentioned Hackerspace being triggered by AC short appearance?
>
Khin doesn’t "trigger". He has a continuous effect based on the number of minions in play.
AC "enters play" effect is a "as played" effect (that’s how crypt cards that are "played" are worded.)
As it is played, it removes itself to do something, so it's never considered to be in play even though it is played, not even for a brief moment.
Timing-wise, this is similar to a contested Elder Library that wouldn't give you +1 hand size, even briefly.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body:
OK, makes sense for Khin, but then Hackerspace text says:

This card comes into play with 1 counter for each Anarch you control. After an Anarch comes into play under your control, or after a vampire you control becomes Anarch, add 1 counter to this card. An Anarch you control can use these counters to pay some or all of the blood or pool cost of an equipment they equip.

If AC still triggers HS, it means AC has to come into play for a moment? Otherwise HS should be worded "After an Anarch is played (...)"?

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
Hackerspace also says "...or after a vampire you control becomes anarch."
Isn't this what triggers Hackerspace in the convert-converts-someone case? Or does Hackerspace trigger twice?

I would personally recommend changing anarch converts text to say:
"As the convert enters play, instead you can remove him from the game to..."

I take notes from how magic handles so called "replacement effects" by using the word "instead". In other words, Event A triggers the ability but the card immediately retcons the situation to say that event B happens instead. So event A never happened even though it triggered the ability. I think Anarch convert would be a perfect candidate for such a wording.
